138	## `auto_zoom`
139	
140	Plans screencast zooms from the clicks and typing in a recording's cursor file, and applies them as one undo step, **Auto Zoom**. It's **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…**. See [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/).
141	
142	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
143	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
144	| `clip` | integer | One of these | A screen recording's media clip. |
145	| `clips` | array of integers | One of these | Media clips whose media have cursor files. |
146	| `zoom` | number | No | How far in, times the clip's own scale: 1.25 to 4. Default: 2. |
147	| `lead` | number | No | Arrive this many seconds before the click: 0.2 to 2. Default: 0.6. |
148	| `stay` | number | No | Stay this many seconds after the last activity: 0.5 to 10. Default: 2.5. |
149	| `follow` | boolean | No | Follows the pointer while zoomed. Default: true. |
150	| `typing` | boolean | No | Zooms on stretches of typing too. Default: true. |
151	| `replace` | boolean | No | Removes the clips' existing zooms first. Default: false. |
152	| `motion_blur` | number | No | The shutter given to each zoomed clip whose own `motion_blur` is 0, as a fraction of a frame: 0 to 1. Default: 0.5, a 180° shutter. 0 sets none. |
153	| `from` | integer | No | Plans only clicks and typing at or after this time, in ticks. With `replace`, removes only zooms that meet the `from` to `to` window. |
154	| `to` | integer | No | Plans only before this time, in ticks. |
155	
156	Each zoom is an ordinary action, the shape `add_zoom_action` makes, so it can be edited like any other. A visit starts at a click, or at a stretch of typing aimed at the last click before it. It zooms in `lead` seconds before that and back out over 0.8 seconds, `stay` seconds after the last activity. [How a visit is planned](/recording/auto-zoom/#how-a-visit-is-planned) has the rest.
157	
158	Halves of a split are planned as one, and nothing straddles a cut. See [Across a split](/recording/auto-zoom/#across-a-split). A planned zoom that meets an action already on the clip is dropped. `replace` removes only zooms, never any other action. A clip that already has a shutter keeps it.
159	
160	It answers as an edit does, and adds:
161	
162	| Key | What it holds |
163	| --- | --- |
164	| `visits` | How many visits were planned. |
165	| `added`, `replaced`, `dropped` | Zooms added, existing zooms removed, and planned zooms dropped because they met an action. |
166	| `closed_at_cut` | Visits closed at a cut, because the later half has an action of its own there. |
167	| `bases_set` | Later halves whose base was set by a zoom held across a cut. |
168	| `blurred` | How many clips were given `motion_blur`. |
169	| `actions` | A list of `{clip, at, duration, kind}`, with `at` in clip ticks and `kind` one of `in`, `pan`, `follow` or `back`. |
170	
171	Besides [the shared rules](#the-tools-that-work-from-a-cursor-file), it won't run when a number is out of range, a clip has no picture, or a clip is placed smaller than the canvas. For that last one, nest the clip, open the nest with `set_scope` and call `auto_zoom` inside it.
172	
173	## `add_shortcut_overlays`
174	
175	Places one Keyboard keys graphic clip for each keyboard shortcut recorded, at the moment it was pressed, as one undo step, **Add Shortcut Overlays**. It's **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays**, which has no sheet, so an agent is the only way to choose these settings. See [Shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/).
176	
177	Only shortcuts are recorded, never typed keys, and only when the recording was made with **Record shortcuts** or `keys: "shortcuts"`. See [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/).
178	
179	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
180	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
181	| `clip` | integer | One of these | A screen recording's media clip. |
182	| `clips` | array of integers | One of these | Media clips whose media have cursor files. |
183	| `duration` | number | No | How long each overlay shows, in seconds: 0.5 to 10. Default: 1.5. |
184	| `position` | string | No | Where the keycaps sit: `bottom` (the default), `center` or `top`. |
185	| `theme` | string | No | The keycaps' look: `dark` (the default) or `light`. |
186	| `from` | integer | No | Places only shortcuts at or after this time, in ticks. |
187	| `to` | integer | No | Places only shortcuts before this time, in ticks. |
188	
189	An overlay never lasts less than 10 frames for each keycap plus 25, the time the template needs to press its last key and exit. Overlays never overlap:
190	
191	- The same shortcut pressed again before its overlay ends extends it, labelled ×2, ×3 and so on.
192	- A different shortcut pressed sooner ends the earlier overlay where it starts, once the earlier one has had its minimum. If that puts it more than 0.5 seconds after its press, it's dropped.
193	
194	The clips go on the front-most track named **Shortcuts** when it's in front of every clip's track, unlocked, shown, not a matte and free over their span. Otherwise they go on a new **Shortcuts** track at the front. A module in `graphics/` whose text equals the bundled template is reused, and otherwise the template is copied in once, only when something is placed.
195	
196	The overlays are ordinary graphic clips. See [Change an overlay](/recording/shortcut-overlays/#change-an-overlay).
197	
198	It answers as an edit does, and adds:
199	
200	| Key | What it holds |
201	| --- | --- |
202	| `added`, `merged`, `dropped` | Overlays placed, repeat presses folded into one, and presses left out. |
203	| `track`, `new_track` | The track used, and whether it's new. |
204	| `module`, `written` | The module drawn, and whether the template was copied in. |
205	| `overlays` | A list of `{at, duration, keys, label}`, with `at` in timeline ticks. |
206	
207	Besides [the shared rules](#the-tools-that-work-from-a-cursor-file), it won't run with a `duration`, `position` or `theme` out of range.
208	
209	## `speed_up_typing`
210	
211	Plays the typing in screen recordings faster, keeping speech and shortcuts at normal speed, as one undo step, **Speed Up Typing**. It's **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…**. See [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/).
212	
213	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
214	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
215	| `clip` | integer | One of these | A screen recording's media clip. |
216	| `clips` | array of integers | One of these | Media clips whose media have cursor files. Halves of a split recording are joined. |
217	| `rate` | number | No | How much faster a stretch plays: 2 to 8. Default: 4. |
218	| `shortest` | number | No | The shortest stretch sped up, in seconds: 1 to 30. Default: 3. |
219	| `keep_pitch` | boolean | No | Keeps the sped sound's pitch. Default: true. |
220	| `from` | integer | No | Speeds only typing at or after this time, in ticks. |
221	| `to` | integer | No | Speeds only typing before this time, in ticks. |
222	
223	A typing stretch is a run of at least 3 typed keys, each under 1 second apart. Taken out of each stretch are every span of speech, in any clip with sound under it on any track, and each recorded shortcut with its overlay, which is 1.5 seconds when it has no clip on a **Shortcuts** track. The pieces of all the clips join where they meet, and a piece shorter than `shortest` is left alone.
224	
225	Each kept piece is sped by `retime_range` at `rate` on every unlocked track, keeping 0.3 seconds at normal speed at each end, so everything after it moves up in step. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
226	
227	Speech detection runs on your Mac. A media with sound under a stretch that has no speech saved yet gets its spans in the same step.
228	
229	It answers `ok`, a `project` summary and the ids it created, and adds:
230	
231	| Key | What it holds |
232	| --- | --- |
233	| `stretches`, `short` | Stretches found, and pieces left alone for being too short. |
234	| `ranges` | A list of `{from, to, sped_to}`, in timeline ticks before the edit. |
235	| `saved` | The time saved, in ticks. |
236	| `speech_saved` | The media whose speech was saved in this step. |
237	| `audio_left_out`, `audio_note` | Only when a clip with sound now plays past ×12, the ceiling for sound. Unlike the menu command, it doesn't ask. See [If a clip would go silent](/recording/speed-up-typing/#if-a-clip-would-go-silent). |
238	
239	Besides [the shared rules](#the-tools-that-work-from-a-cursor-file), it won't run, and nothing changes, when:
240	
241	- `rate` or `shortest` is out of range.
242	- `retime_range` would refuse any range, because of a locked track after it, a transition or a linked clip, for example. The sentence names it.
243	- Speech detection is still running. It doesn't wait, and it says to try again in a moment.
244	
245	## Related
246	
247	- [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/)
248	- [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/)
249	- [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/)
250	- [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/)

1	---
2	title: "Tools: rendering and export"
3	description: "The agent tools that render one frame of the timeline, start an export, follow it on the Export Queue and stop it."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These tools turn the timeline into pictures and files. `render_frame` is how an agent sees what it has done, and `export`, `export_status` and `cancel_export` write the finished file.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['File ▸ Save Frame…', 'File ▸ Export…', 'Window ▸ Export Queue']}
12	  keys="⌘E"
13	  tools={['render_frame', 'export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
14	  needs="A client connected over MCP, or the Assistant tab."
15	/>
16	
17	Each tool has a heading here with its arguments. [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/) and [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/) walk through using them.
18	
19	Every tool here also takes `project`, the path of an open project. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/). None of them takes `scope`.
20	
21	## `render_frame`
22	
23	Renders one frame of the finished timeline as a picture the model can see and a file on disk. It goes through the same composition and compositor an export does, so it shows what the file will hold at that moment. Use it before and after every edit. It's the same writer as **File ▸ Save Frame…**, so a PNG written here and one saved from the menu are byte-identical. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).
24	
25	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
26	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
27	| `t` | integer | No | The moment to render, in ticks, rounded to the frame grid. Default: the playhead. |
28	| `path` | string | No | Where to write the file. The folder must exist. Default: a temporary file. |
29	| `format` | string | No | `png`, `jpeg` or `heic`. Default: the path's own extension when it's one of those, else `png`. An explicit format wins, and the path's extension is replaced, so `shot.jpg` with `png` writes `shot.png`. |
30	| `max_width` | integer | No | Caps the image's width, 16 to 8192 pixels, aspect kept and never scaled up. Default: the canvas's own size. |
31	| `burn_in_timecode` | boolean | No | Draws the project timecode over the picture, topmost. Default: false. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/). |
32	| `ungraded` | boolean | No | Draws as if no clip were graded, which is **View ▸ Show Ungraded**'s picture. Default: false. See [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/). |
33	| `sdr_version` | boolean | No | Draws an HDR project's SDR version, which is **View ▸ Show SDR Version**'s picture. An SDR project's frame doesn't change. Default: false. See [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/). |
34	| `selection` | integer | No | An adjustment clip's id. Draws what its qualifier selects, which is **View ▸ Show Selection**'s picture: grey, white fully graded and black untouched, with every layer in front of the clip left out. Black where the clip isn't on the frame. See [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/). |
35	| `waveform` | boolean | No | Also measures the frame's luma waveform. Default: false. |
36	| `parade` | boolean | No | Also measures the frame's RGB parade. Default: false. |
37	| `vectorscope` | boolean | No | Also measures the frame's vectorscope. Default: false. |
38	| `vectorscope_zoom` | integer | No | The vectorscope's zoom: 1, 2 or 4. Needs `vectorscope: true`. Default: 1. |
39	| `histogram` | boolean | No | Also measures the frame's histogram. Default: false. |
40	
41	The view switches themselves never reach this tool, so an agent asks for each picture here, whatever a person has switched on.
42	
43	It answers an image block and a text block. The text says the moment, the canvas's size and the size it rendered at, and its last sentence is "Written to `<path>`." Before that last sentence it can add:
44	
45	- A note that a JPEG flattened a transparent canvas onto black. PNG and HEIC keep the canvas's transparency.
46	- A graphic that warned or failed, naming it, its frame and the problem. A failed graphic draws its error card in the picture.
47	- A recorded cursor that couldn't be drawn: "The cursor of media M is not drawn:" and why. The clip draws without one.
48	- A clip with Remove Background whose masks weren't ready. It waits up to 30 seconds, then draws the clip uncut and names it.
49	- What each scope measured.
50	
51	**Scopes.** Each scope you ask for adds a sentence and writes a JSON file beside the image, named `<image path>.waveform.json`, `.parade.json`, `.vectorscope.json` or `.histogram.json`. The waveform and histogram sentences give the share of pixels clipping high and low, the parade gives it for each channel, and the vectorscope gives the share that's neutral. The waveform, parade and vectorscope count into 256 × 256 bins, and the histogram into 256 levels. At zoom 2 or 4, pixels off the vectorscope's plot aren't counted, and the text says what share they are. See [Scopes](/color/scopes/).
52	
53	**In an HDR project,** the frame is a 16-bit PNG or a 10-bit HEIC labelled BT.2100 HLG. A JPEG, and any frame asked for with `sdr_version`, is the project's SDR version, labelled BT.709. Scopes read the picture drawn, so the HLG signal adds `signal: "hlg"` to each JSON file.
54	
55	**With a nest open,** it renders that nest, at its own canvas and from its own zero, which is what the preview is showing. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
56	
57	It won't render when:
58	
59	- `selection` isn't an adjustment clip of the project.
60	- `vectorscope_zoom` isn't 1, 2 or 4, or comes without `vectorscope: true`.
61	- `max_width` or `format` is out of range, `path` is empty, or the folder doesn't exist.
62	- There's no frame at that time, because it's past the end, the media is missing or the timeline is empty.
63	
64	## `export`
65	
66	Puts the timeline on the Export Queue and answers at once, as **File ▸ Export…** (<kbd>⌘E</kbd>) does with its sheet. It takes everything on the sheet but the frame rate: an export runs at the project's rate, or at 12.5 fps for `gif` and 25 fps for `apng`. An agent's export and a menu export go through the same exporter. See [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/).
67	
68	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
69	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
70	| `preset` | string | Yes | The encoding, one of the [presets](#the-presets). A wrong one is refused with the full list. |
71	| `path` | string | Yes | Where to write. The folder must exist. The format's extension is added when the path has none, and an existing file is replaced. |
72	| `size` | string or array of 2 integers | No | The sheet's **Size**: `document`, `720p`, `1080p`, `1440p`, `2160p`, `preset` (`gif` and `apng` only), or `[width, height]` in pixels, 16 to 8192 on each edge. Default: the document's size, or the format's cap on `gif` and `apng`. See [Export size](/export/size/). |
73	| `range` | string | No | `project` (the default) for the whole timeline, or `in_out` for the range `set_range` set. |
74	| `video_bitrate` | integer | No | Target video rate in bits per second, 1 or more, so 8000000 is 8 Mbps. Default: the preset decides. ProRes, `gif` and `apng` ignore it, and on AV1 and VP9 it's a soft cap. See [Export quality](/export/quality/). |
75	| `audio_bitrate` | integer | No | Target AAC or Opus rate in bits per second, 1 or more. Default: 192 kbps. ProRes, WAV and AIFF ignore it. |
76	| `audio_bits` | integer | No | `audio_wav`'s and `audio_aiff`'s bit depth, 16 or 24. Default: 16. Refused on every other preset. See [Export bit depth](/export/bit-depth/). |
77	| `loudness_lufs` | number | No | Normalises the whole mix to this integrated loudness, −70 to 0 LUFS. The sheet's rows are −14, −16 and −23. Omit it not to normalise. Ignored by `gif` and `apng`. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/). |
78	| `peak_dbtp` | number | No | The ceiling of the master limiter every export with sound runs, −20 to 0 dBTP. Default: −1. There's no off. |
79	| `burn_in_timecode` | boolean | No | Draws the project timecode over the picture. It shows project time even in a range export. Default: false. |
80	| `dynamic_range` | string | No | An HDR project's picture on `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422` and `prores_4444`: `hlg` (the default), `pq` for HDR10, or `sdr`. Every other video preset writes the SDR version. See [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/). |
81	| `encoder_speed` | string | No | `av1`'s and `av1_webm`'s speed: `faster`, `balanced` (the default) or `smaller`. Refused on every other preset. See [Encoder speed](/export/encoder-speed/). |
82	| `stems` | string | No | Also writes stems beside the mix on the three audio presets: `tracks` for one file per heard track, or `names` for one per track name. See [Audio stems](/export/stems/). |
83	
84	### The presets
85	
86	A preset is a container and a codec, with no size of its own.
87	
88	| Preset | Writes | Good to know |
89	| --- | --- | --- |
90	| `h264` | H.264 in MP4 | 8-bit. What the export sheet opens on. |
91	| `hevc` | HEVC in MP4 | 8-bit. |
92	| `hevc_10bit` | HEVC in MP4 | 10-bit. |
93	| `hevc_alpha` | HEVC with alpha in MOV | 8-bit. Keeps a transparent canvas. Safari's transparent movie. |
94	| `av1` | AV1 in MP4 with AAC | 10-bit. Macs before M3 can't play it back. |
95	| `av1_webm` | AV1 in WebM with Opus | 10-bit. Macs before M3 can't play it back. |
96	| `vp9_webm` | VP9 in WebM with Opus | 8-bit for an SDR picture, 10-bit for HLG and PQ. |
97	| `vp9_alpha_webm` | VP9 with alpha in WebM with Opus | Always 8-bit. Keeps a transparent canvas. The transparent movie Chrome and Firefox play. |
98	| `prores_422` | ProRes 422 in MOV | 10-bit. |
99	| `prores_4444` | ProRes 4444 in MOV | 12-bit. Keeps a transparent canvas. |
100	| `audio_m4a` | AAC in M4A | Sound only. |
101	| `audio_wav` | WAV | Sound only. |
102	| `audio_aiff` | AIFF | Sound only. |
103	| `gif` | Animated GIF | Can show a transparent pixel, but nothing partial survives. |
104	| `apng` | Animated PNG | Keeps a transparent canvas. |
105	
106	See [Choose a format](/export/formats/) for what each is for.
107	
108	### What it answers
109	
110	`export` answers `{export_id, path, status}` at once, and `status` is `queued` or `running`. The job runs one at a time behind any other export already on the queue. An `av1`, `av1_webm` or `vp9_webm` job also waits while the app's other AV1 and VP9 exports would hold more than a quarter of this Mac's memory with it, and a later job may run first meanwhile. The queue window isn't opened. The export always writes the whole document, even with a nest open.
111	
112	Follow it with [`export_status`](#export_status) and stop it with [`cancel_export`](#cancel_export). The `export_id` lasts until Frame Job quits.
113	
114	### When it refuses
115	
116	Every refusal comes back from this call, before anything is queued. `export` won't start when:
117	
118	- There's nothing on the timeline.
119	- `range` is `in_out` and the project has no in and out range.
120	- `preset` is unknown, or `size` isn't a row or a pair of edges from 16 to 8192. Each sentence lists what it takes.
121	- `size` is a `[width, height]` of a different shape from the canvas on `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha` or `vp9_alpha_webm`, because padding would destroy the alpha those presets are chosen for.
122	- `size` is `preset` on anything but `gif` or `apng`.
123	- `audio_bits` or `encoder_speed` is on a preset that doesn't take it.
124	- `dynamic_range` is `hlg` or `pq` on a preset that can't write it, or in an SDR project, where `sdr` changes nothing.
125	- `stems` is on a movie preset, or no track can be heard.
126	- The folder doesn't exist.
127	- A graphic clip's module doesn't compile.
128	
129	A failure while writing comes back from `export_status` instead. That includes a graphic that fails during the export, which stops it with no file left and names the graphic and the frame, and a stem whose file would replace media the project uses.
130	
131	## `export_status`
132	
133	Answers how an export is going. It's the job's row in **Window ▸ Export Queue**, read now. It never waits, so call it again after a pause until `status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
134	
135	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
136	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
137	| `export_id` | integer | Yes | The `export_id` that `export` answered, 1 or more. |
138	
139	Every answer has `export_id`, `status`, `path` and `elapsed`, the seconds since `export` was called, or up to the finish once it has finished. The rest depends on `status`:
140	
141	| Status | Adds |
142	| --- | --- |
143	| `queued` | `waiting`, the queue row's sentence, while the job waits for memory behind other AV1 and VP9 exports. |
144	| `queued` or `running` | `estimated_seconds` on `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`: the export sheet's estimate of the whole write, in whole seconds. |
145	| `running` | `progress`, 0 to 1, and `phase` while the exporter names one, such as the loudness measurement. |
146	| `done` | What the file holds, below. |
147	| `failed`, `cancelled` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |
148	
149	When it's `done`, it adds:
150	
151	| Key | What it holds |
152	| --- | --- |
153	| `ok`, `bytes` | True, and the file's size. |
154	| `preset`, `container`, `codec`, `width`, `height`, `fps`, `start`, `duration` | The settings used. `fps` is `[num, den]`, and the width and height are the file's. |
155	| `burn_in_timecode` | Whether the burn-in was asked for. |
156	| `dynamic_range` | In an HDR project, the picture written. |
157	| `encoder_speed` | On `av1` and `av1_webm`. |
158	| `audio_bits` | On `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. |
159	| `stems` | With `stems`, a list of `{name, tracks, path}`, one for each file beside the mix. |
160	| `loudness` | For every format that carries sound, normalised or not: `summary`, `integrated_lufs`, `true_peak_dbtp`, `sample_peak_dbfs`, `gain_db`, `ceiling_dbtp`, `limited_db`, `capped_by_gain`, and `target_lufs` when one was asked for. Absent when there was no sound to measure. |
161	| `graphic_warnings` | A list of `{name, frame, message}`, each distinct warning a graphic gave while the file was drawn. Absent when there were none. |
162	| `cursor_warnings` | A list of `{media, path, message}`, each media whose cursor file couldn't be drawn, so its clips drew without one. Absent when there were none. |
163	
164	`integrated_lufs` is absent for a programme too short or too quiet to have one, and `summary` says so in words. `limited_db` says how far the limiter turned the hottest peak down, and `capped_by_gain` is true when the +40 dB gain cap decided the gain.
165	
166	Only ids `export` answered since Frame Job launched are known. Anything else is refused, and that includes a job a person put on the queue. A finished job's answer outlives its queue row, so it still reads after **Remove** or **Clear Finished**.
167	
168	## `cancel_export`
169	
170	Stops an export, as **Cancel** in its Export Queue row does. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).
171	
172	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
173	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
174	| `export_id` | integer | Yes | The `export_id` that `export` answered, 1 or more. |
175	
176	A queued export is cancelled before it starts. A running one stops and its half-written file is removed, though the answer may still read `running` until the writer has stopped, when `export_status` reads `cancelled`. A finished export is left alone.
177	
178	It answers as `export_status` does, and it refuses an id `export` didn't answer since launch.
179	
180	## Related
181	
182	- [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/)
183	- [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/)
184	- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)
185	- [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/)

==================== add_shortcut_overlays
Places one Keyboard keys graphic clip per keyboard shortcut recorded in screen recordings' cursor files, at the moment it was pressed, as ONE undo step "Add Shortcut Overlays" — Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays. Only shortcuts are recorded (Record shortcuts in the recorder), never typed keys. Each press inside a clip's played window is placed through the clip's speed and ramps, snapped to the frame grid. An overlay lasts duration seconds and never less than (10 × keycaps + 25) frames, the time the template needs to press its last key and exit. The same shortcut pressed again before its overlay ends extends it to duration after the last press, labelled ×2, ×3 … (merged counts them); a different shortcut pressed sooner ends the earlier overlay where it starts, waiting until the earlier one has had its minimum — and if that is more than 0.5 s after its press it is dropped (dropped counts them). Overlays never overlap. They go on the front-most track named "Shortcuts" when it is in front of every clip's track, unlocked, shown, not a matte and free over their span; otherwise on a new "Shortcuts" track at the front (new_track). The project's graphics/ module whose text equals the bundled keyboard-keys template is reused; otherwise the template is copied in once (written), and only when something is placed. Refused: a clip that is not a media clip, whose media has no cursor file or whose file is missing, or that plays reversed. Answers added, dropped, merged, track, new_track, module, written and overlays [{at, duration, keys, label}] (at in container ticks); with no shortcut in the clips' played windows, ok with a note and no undo step.

==================== speed_up_typing
Plays the typing in screen recordings faster, as ONE undo step "Speed Up Typing" — Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…. A typing stretch is a run of at least 3 typed keys each under 1 s apart, read from the clips' cursor files and placed through each clip's speed and ramps. From each stretch is taken away every span of speech of every clip with sound under it, on any track, and each recorded shortcut with its overlay (its clip on a track named "Shortcuts", else 1.5 s), so speech and shortcut overlays always play at normal speed. The pieces of all the clips are joined where they meet, a piece shorter than shortest seconds is left alone (short counts them), and each kept piece is sped by retime_range at rate on every unlocked track, keeping 0.3 s at normal speed at each end, so everything after it moves up in step. Its sound is sped too, its pitch kept with keep_pitch. A media with sound under a stretch whose speech has not been saved gets its spans from on-device speech detection in the same step (speech_saved); while detection runs the call is refused — try again in a moment. Refused, whole and before anything changes: a clip that is not a media clip, whose media has no cursor file or whose file is missing, or that plays reversed; a rate or shortest out of range; any range retime_range would refuse (a locked track after it, a transition, a linked clip …), naming it. Answers stretches, short, ranges [{from, to, sped_to}] in container ticks before the edit, saved (ticks), speech_saved and, when a clip with sound is now above the audio ceiling, audio_left_out and audio_note; with nothing to speed, ok with a note and no undo step.

==================== record_screen
Records the screen for seconds and lands the movie as ORDINARY MEDIA — File ▸ New Recording…, without the panel. The file goes to ~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings (or the folder path names), named Screen Recording <date> at <time>.mov, and is then imported as import_media imports a file — a media entry — and, with place (the default), placed at the playhead on the front track of whatever container is open (inside a nest when set_scope has one open), or, when that track has no room there, on a new track in front of everything; a paused recording lands one clip per segment (below). With no project open, or when the target document closed while the recording ran, it opens as a NEW untitled project instead and landed says new_project; that document is then addressable by project: <the recording's path>, which is the path get_project reports for it. The canvas of that new project takes rate, while the media record keeps the file's OWN frame rate — for a screen recording that is whatever the screen did, since ScreenCaptureKit delivers a frame only when something changes, so a mostly-still screen reports a low, fractional fps; that is the file, not a defect, and the picture holds its last frame to the end of the sound. A microphone is a SECOND file (<stem> (Microphone).m4a) landing as a second clip on a new back track named Microphone, at the picture's start minus mic_offset — the measured lead of one file over the other, in ticks, positive meaning the picture began after the microphone; a negative start is the head trimmed, not a clip placed late. A microphone that never started, whose writer failed or whose file will not read does NOT fail the recording: the picture lands, that segment's mic_path and mic ids are absent, and mic_problem carries the sentence (the note repeats it)

233	   233	    /// Start, the span, stop. See the header for the hook and the waits. A

239	   239	    private func record(
240	   240	        filter: SCContentFilter?, choice: RecordingChoice, seconds: Double, cameraBeside: Bool
241	   241	    ) throws -> RecordingResult {
242	   242	        let recorder = ScreenRecorder.shared
243	   243	        let started = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0)
244	   244	        let startBox = AgentBox<Result<Void, Error>>()
245	   245	        let finished = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0)
246	   246	        let box = AgentBox<Result<RecordingResult, Error>>()
247	   247	        let chrome = RecordingToolChrome()
248	   248	        // `onFinish` runs on MAIN, once: the status item comes down before
249	   249	        // the landing, and the box is written before the signal.
250	   250	        let deliver: (Result<RecordingResult, Error>) -> Void = { outcome in
251	   251	            chrome.remove()
252	   252	            if box.value == nil { box.value = outcome }
253	   253	            finished.signal()
254	   254	        }
255	   255	        let startCompletion: (Error?) -> Void = { error in
256	   256	            startBox.value = error.map { .failure($0) } ?? .success(())
257	   257	            started.signal()
258	   258	        }
259	   259	        onMain {
260	   260	            if let filter {
261	   261	                recorder.start(
262	   262	                    filter: filter, choice: choice, mayAsk: false, onFinish: deliver,
263	   263	                    completion: startCompletion)
264	   264	            } else if choice.source == .camera {
265	   265	                recorder.startCamera(
266	   266	                    choice: choice, mayAsk: false, onFinish: deliver,
267	   267	                    completion: startCompletion)
268	   268	            } else {
269	   269	                recorder.startVoiceOver(
270	   270	                    choice: choice, mayAsk: false, onFinish: deliver,
271	   271	                    completion: startCompletion)
272	   272	            }
273	   273	        }
274	   274	        // The recorder's own arm timer answers first; this bound is for a
275	   275	        // start that never answers at all.
276	   276	        guard started.wait(timeout: .now() + ScreenRecorder.armCeiling + 5) == .success else {
277	   277	            throw ToolError(
278	   278	                message: "record_screen timed out waiting for the recording to start."
279	   279	                    + Self.recordingAlertClause)
280	   280	        }
281	   281	        if case .failure(let error) = startBox.value ?? .success(()) {
282	   282	            throw ToolError(message: Self.startSentence(of: error))
283	   283	        }
284	   284	        onMain { chrome.show(recorder) }
285	   285	        if filter == nil { awaitFirstStart(recorder, ended: box) }

302	   302	                // a camera file beside each movie that has one.

305	   305	                    chrome.remove()

308	   308	                }

310	   310	                    message: Self.finishTimeoutSentence(
311	   311	                        movies: movies, cameras: cameras, camera: cameraBeside,
312	   312	                        voiceOver: choice.source == .voiceOver))

==================== auto_zoom
Plans screencast zooms from screen recordings' cursor files and applies them as ONE undo step "Auto Zoom" — Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…. Each zoom is an ordinary action (add_zoom_action's shape). A visit starts at a down click (or, with typing, a typing stretch, aimed at the last click before it): a zoom-in arriving lead seconds before it, a pan for each later click outside the zoomed region's inner 60 %, with follow a 0.5 s pan when the pointer stays outside the inner 70 % for 0.3 s, and a 0.8 s zoom back stay seconds after the last activity (or at a scroll burst). A click within stay of the last joins the visit; a zoom back that would end under 1 s before the next zoom-in becomes a pan. The region has the canvas's aspect at zoom × the clip's scale, kept inside the picture. Halves of a split are planned as one: every zoom back ends at the first half's placement, nothing straddles a cut, and a zoom held across a cut sets the later half's base (bases_set) unless it has an action of its own there, when the visit closes at the cut (closed_at_cut). A planned zoom meeting an action already on the clip is dropped (dropped); with replace the clips' existing zooms are removed first (replaced) and never any other action. Each clip given a zoom whose own motion_blur is 0 is set to motion_blur (0.5 by default, a 180° shutter; set_video's key, drawn along the zooms) in the same step — blurred counts them; 0 sets none, and a clip that already has a shutter keeps it. Refused: a clip that is not a media clip, whose media has no cursor file or whose file is missing, that plays reversed, has no picture, or is placed smaller than the canvas (nest it and call auto_zoom inside the nest with set_scope). Answers visits, added, replaced, dropped, closed_at_cut, bases_set, blurred and actions [{clip, at, duration, kind}] (at in clip ticks; kind in, pan, follow or back); with nothing to zoom, ok with a note and no undo step.
==================== record_screen
Records the screen for seconds and lands the movie as ORDINARY MEDIA — File ▸ New Recording…, without the panel. The file goes to ~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings (or the folder path names), named Screen Recording <date> at <time>.mov, and is then imported as import_media imports a file — a media entry — and, with place (the default), placed at the playhead on the front track of whatever container is open (inside a nest when set_scope has one open), or, when that track has no room there, on a new track in front of everything; a paused recording lands one clip per segment (below). With no project open, or when the target document closed while the recording ran, it opens as a NEW untitled project instead and landed says new_project; that document is then addressable by project: <the recording's path>, which is the path get_project reports for it. The canvas of that new project takes rate, while the media record keeps the file's OWN frame rate — for a screen recording that is whatever the screen did, since ScreenCaptureKit delivers a frame only when something changes, so a mostly-still screen reports a low, fractional fps; that is the file, not a defect, and the picture holds its last frame to the end of the sound. A microphone is a SECOND file (<stem> (Microphone).m4a) landing as a second clip on a new back track named Microphone, at the picture's start minus mic_offset — the measured lead of one file over the other, in ticks, positive meaning the picture began after the microphone; a negative start is the head trimmed, not a clip placed late. A microphone that never started, whose writer failed or whose file will not read does NOT fail the recording: the picture lands, that segment's mic_path and mic ids are absent, and mic_problem carries the sentence (the note repeats it). THE GRANTS: this tool never asks for one and never opens the picker. The Screen Recording grant (and the Microphone grant when microphone is true, and the Camera grant for source camera or a camera beside the screen) must already be held by this process — the panel is where somebody grants them — and a missing one is refused by name with the System Settings pane in the sentence. A Frame Job launched from a shell runs under the TERMINAL's grants, not the app icon's, and both refusals then also name the launching process (its pid) and the way out — relaunch with open -a "Frame Job", or grant the terminal. THE REFUSAL ORDER is fixed: your own mistakes first (seconds missing or outside 1…600, a source outside the vocabulary and the arguments that source refuses, display and window both given, a rate or size outside the vocabulary, enhance: true without a microphone and then with place: false, auto_zoom, shortcut_overlays and speed_up_typing each with place: false and the last two without keys: shortcuts, a camera_layout outside the vocabulary, camera_layout and then camera_cutout: true with place: false, microphone: true without the Microphone grant, a project naming nothing open), then for a camera recording or a camera beside the screen the camera lookup, then its camera_format, then the Camera grant, then for a screen recording the Screen Recording grant, then the display or window lookup — where a console that is locked or asleep lists NO display and is refused as that, by name; then the recording itself. While it records, a status item in the menu bar shows the elapsed time with a menu offering Pause Recording and Stop Recording — Resume Recording and Stop Recording while it is paused — and File ▸ Pause Recording (Resume Recording while paused) and File ▸ Stop Recording work too. A person's Stop from the menu bar or the File menu ends an agent's recording EARLY and it still lands, with stopped_by: stopped — the same value the tool's own stop at the span's end yields — and a duration shorter than the span, which is what says so; user_stopped is only the SYSTEM's own screen-recording indicator, and system_stopped a display that slept or a camera that stopped on its own. PAUSE: the span is wall clock, so a person's pause SHORTENS what the call records — the paused stretch is in no file — and the result's pauses says how many times Pause was pressed (0 when never; a pause with no resume before the stop still counts). A paused recording is a SEQUENCE of files, one per stretch between a start or resume and a pause or the stop, each named by its own start time and, with a microphone, carrying its own microphone file with its own measured mic_offset; every segment lands as its own clip placed at the previous one's end on ONE track, touching and never overlapping, and each microphone file as its own clip on the Microphone track at its own offset. segments carries one entry per file (exactly one for an unpaused recording) and duration is the TOTAL recorded across them. A segment whose movie will not read (an empty file, from a pause in the instant after a resume), or whose writer failed after the segment closed, is LEFT OUT rather than failing the recording: the readable segments land, and the result's unreadable lists each one left out — path, kept_files (what it left on disk), reason, and mic_path, mic_duration, mic_media and mic_clip when its microphone file reads, which lands without its picture in the slot the picture would have had — with the note naming them; only a recording with NO readable movie fails, naming every file. The call blocks for seconds plus about a second of start and finish, and up to 75 s more if the writers are slow to close the files — 60 s more for each further segment of a paused recording, whose files are probed in turn; a timeout names the movies, which may still finish on their own. THE RESULT carries: path (the FIRST segment's movie — the recording's file, the one a new project is addressed by); mic_offset (ALWAYS present — the first segment's, 0 without a microphone); mic_path and mic_duration (the first segment's) when its microphone file landed, and mic_problem — every segment's sentence, joined — when a microphone was asked for and any segment's did not land, which can stand beside a mic_path when it was a later segment's; media and clip (the first segment's ids; clip and mic_clip absent with place: false), mic_media and mic_clip (its microphone's); duration (ticks — the TOTAL recorded, every segment's summed, which for an unpaused recording is the movie's own); width, height, fps [num, den], has_audio and audio_tracks — the FIRST segment's movie's (what it holds: audio_tracks is 1 with system_audio, else 0 — the microphone is never a track of it); pauses (an integer, the count of Pause presses); segments (an array, ALWAYS present, one entry per file in order, each with path, duration, started_at — the screen's own start as an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp to the millisecond — its OWN width, height and fps, because a screen recording's rate is whatever the screen did and differs per segment, and mic_path, mic_duration, mic_offset and mic_problem on the same terms as the top level for THAT segment's files, plus media, clip, mic_media and mic_clip when they are known); stopped_by — stopped for the tool's own stop and for a person's Stop from Frame Job's menu-bar item or the File menu, user_stopped for the system's own screen-recording indicator, system_stopped for a display that slept or a camera that stopped on its own; landed (document or new_project); note, when there is something to say; project, the usual summary; and for a document landing the created ids as every edit reports them — new_media, new_clips, and new_tracks when a track was minted — plus scope and document_ops when it landed inside a nest. A failure AFTER the files were written names every one of them: "The recording was saved at <path> but could not be added: …", the movies comma-separated and the microphone files after them. UNDO: for a document landing, undo removes every segment's media and clip(s) in ONE step and leaves the files on disk, as undoing Add Media… does; a recording that opened as a new project has no undo step for its first segment — that picture IS the document — and with a microphone on an unpaused recording, undo removes the microphone pair (the step is named Add Microphone) and leaves the picture, while a PAUSED recording's later segments and every microphone clip are one step named Add Recording Segments, so undo leaves the first picture alone in the document. A VOICE-OVER: source: "voice_over" records the DEFAULT microphone alone — the panel's Source row Microphone Only — with no picture, into files named Voice-over <date> at <time>.m4a, one file per stretch between pauses. Every file lands touching, from the playhead, on ONE new back track named Microphone, in one undo step (Add Recording); as a new project the first file IS the document, 1920×1080 at rate, and the later files touch it on its one track. display, window, system_audio, show_clicks, size and include_framejob_windows are refused by name with source voice_over, and so is microphone: false (true is implied); source is read right after seconds, and only the Microphone grant is read — never the Screen Recording one. The result's path is the first .m4a, its width and height 0, with no mic_path, and mic_offset 0; a microphone that stops on its own ends the voice-over, what it wrote lands, and mic_problem and the note say so. A CAMERA: source: "camera" records a camera alone, with no screen — the one camera names (a device's unique id, or its name in any case), else the default camera (the system's preferred camera, else the first built-in, else the first) — at its best format (the largest size wider than tall at 30 fps or more, at that format's highest rate) or the one camera_format names (a format the camera lacks is refused naming its formats), into files named Camera Recording <date> at <time>.mov, one file per stretch between pauses; microphone: true adds the DEFAULT microphone as a second file, as for a screen. It lands as a screen recording's picture does; as a new project the canvas is the file's size at the format's rate, rounded. display, window, system_audio, show_clicks, size, include_framejob_windows and rate are refused by name with source camera, and camera and camera_format with source voice_over. The camera is looked up after project — an unknown one is refused naming every camera connected, and "No camera is connected." when there is none — and only then is the Camera grant read, never the Screen Recording one. The span counts from the camera's first frame, after it settles at its rate (up to a second). The result carries camera: {name, id, format, problem, note} — format spelled 1920x1080@30; camera.problem the sentence of a camera that stopped on its own, which ends the recording with stopped_by: system_stopped and lands what it wrote; camera.note when the camera had not settled at its rate when the recording began; each of the two also said in the note — and has_audio false: the movie holds no sound. A CAMERA BESIDE THE SCREEN: source: "screen" (the default) with camera records that camera at the same time as the screen — camera_format as for source camera, refused without camera — one <movie stem> (Camera).mov per segment beside each movie. The camera files land in the same undo step, on ONE new track named Camera in FRONT of the screen's, one clip per segment at its screen clip's start plus that segment's camera_offset (ticks, positive when the camera began after the screen; it is usually negative, a camera starting first, and then the clip's head is trimmed rather than the clip placed early), never before its screen clip and never overlapping the camera clip before it. Each camera clip lands in camera_layout's layout by one switch_layout at its first frame, one frame long, with its segment's screen clip as the screen and reaching no further than the later of the two clips' ends: corner_square (the default) is the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner — scaled to fit a quarter of the canvas wide and a third of it tall, inside the 90 % safe-area ring — and a segment whose screen clip is missing or does not play at the camera's start gets that corner by set_video x, y and scale instead; either way it stays an ordinary clip to move. With camera_cutout: true the camera clips then get Remove Background as their own undo step before any enhance, and the answer carries camera_cutout {clips} or camera_cutout_error, the sentence when no camera clip landed. The microphone, when asked for, is its own file on the Microphone track as for any screen recording. With place: false the camera files are media with no clip and no Camera track. As a new project the first movie is the document and the camera lands in its remainder step — named Add Camera, or Add Camera and Microphone with a voice, for one segment. Each entry of segments then also carries camera_path, camera_duration and camera_offset when that segment's camera file landed, camera_problem and camera_note when set (also said in the note), and camera_media and camera_clip when known; the top-level camera is as for source camera. A segment left out because its movie will not read keeps its camera file on disk, named in its kept_files, and does not land it. The stop wait allows 105 s, and 90 s more for each further segment, because the camera's file is probed too, and a timeout names the camera files after the movies. The recorder panel's Record the camera too box, with a display or a window, makes the same recording, and its Layout pop-up and Remove the camera's background when it lands box are camera_layout and camera_cutout. ENHANCE: enhance: true runs enhance_voice over the recording's MICROPHONE clips — each segment's microphone file, or a voice-over's files; never the picture, a camera or the system audio — once their loudness and speech have been analysed, at −16 LUFS, as its OWN undo step named Enhance Voice after the landing's (undo takes the processing off and keeps the recording). The call waits for that analysis, up to 5 minutes, and the answer then also carries enhance — enhance_voice's own answer — or enhance_error, a sentence saying why it did not run (nothing measurable, no microphone clip on the timeline, or not analysed within 5 minutes); project is read after it. The landing itself is the same either way. The recorder panel's Enhance the microphone when it lands box does the same. CURSOR: every display, window or picked recording also writes the pointer's path, clicks, scrolls and the frames' geometry beside each segment movie as <movie stem>.fjcursor (the pointer is still in the picture too). Each entry of segments then also carries cursor_path and cursor_image ("none": no cursor image is recorded) when that segment's cursor file was written, and cursor_problem when it was not or holds only the geometry the screen had when the segment began (also said in the note); a cursor problem never fails the recording. WHEN IT LANDS: auto_zoom, shortcut_overlays and speed_up_typing run auto_zoom, add_shortcut_overlays and speed_up_typing over the recording's SCREEN clips (each segment's movie whose media has a cursor file) after the landing and after any enhance, in that order, each as its OWN undo step named Auto Zoom, Add Shortcut Overlays and Speed Up Typing, with those tools' defaults and no from or to. speed_up_typing waits for the clips' speech to be detected, up to 5 minutes. The answer then also carries each one's own answer under its name, or a sentence under <name>_error saying why it did not run (no screen clip with a cursor file, the project busy or the speech not detected within 5 minutes, the call stopped, or the tool's own refusal); project is read after them. The recorder panel's When it lands boxes — Zoom in on clicks, Show shortcuts and Speed up typing — do the same.

==================== auto_zoom
Plans screencast zooms from screen recordings' cursor files and applies them as ONE undo step "Auto Zoom" — Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…. Each zoom is an ordinary action (add_zoom_action's shape). A visit starts at a down click (or, with typing, a typing stretch, aimed at the last click before it): a zoom-in arriving lead seconds before it, a pan for each later click outside the zoomed region's inner 60 %, with follow a 0.5 s pan when the pointer stays outside the inner 70 % for 0.3 s, and a 0.8 s zoom back stay seconds after the last activity (or at a scroll burst). A click within stay of the last joins the visit; a zoom back that would end under 1 s before the next zoom-in becomes a pan. The region has the canvas's aspect at zoom × the clip's scale, kept inside the picture. Halves of a split are planned as one: every zoom back ends at the first half's placement, nothing straddles a cut, and a zoom held across a cut sets the later half's base (bases_set) unless it has an action of its own there, when the visit closes at the cut (closed_at_cut). A planned zoom meeting an action already on the clip is dropped (dropped); with replace the clips' existing zooms are removed first (replaced) and never any other action. Each clip given a zoom whose own motion_blur is 0 is set to motion_blur (0.5 by default, a 180° shutter; set_video's key, drawn along the zooms) in the same step — blurred counts them; 0 sets none, and a clip that already has a shutter keeps it. Refused: a clip that is not a media clip, whose media has no cursor file or whose file is missing, that plays reversed, has no picture, or is placed smaller than the canvas (nest it and call auto_zoom inside the nest with set_scope). Answers visits, added, replaced, dropped, closed_at_cut, bases_set, blurred and actions [{clip, at, duration, kind}] (at in clip ticks; kind in, pan, follow or back); with nothing to zoom, ok with a note and no undo step.
==================== record_screen
Records the screen for seconds and lands the movie as ORDINARY MEDIA — File ▸ New Recording…, without the panel. The file goes to ~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings (or the folder path names), named Screen Recording <date> at <time>.mov, and is then imported as import_media imports a file — a media entry — and, with place (the default), placed at the playhead on the front track of whatever container is open (inside a nest when set_scope has one open), or, when that track has no room there, on a new track in front of everything; a paused recording lands one clip per segment (below). With no project open, or when the target document closed while the recording ran, it opens as a NEW untitled project instead and landed says new_project; that document is then addressable by project: <the recording's path>, which is the path get_project reports for it. The canvas of that new project takes rate, while the media record keeps the file's OWN frame rate — for a screen recording that is whatever the screen did, since ScreenCaptureKit delivers a frame only when something changes, so a mostly-still screen reports a low, fractional fps; that is the file, not a defect, and the picture holds its last frame to the end of the sound. A microphone is a SECOND file (<stem> (Microphone).m4a) landing as a second clip on a new back track named Microphone, at the picture's start minus mic_offset — the measured lead of one file over the other, in ticks, positive meaning the picture began after the microphone; a negative start is the head trimmed, not a clip placed late. A microphone that never started, whose writer failed or whose file will not read does NOT fail the recording: the picture lands, that segment's mic_path and mic ids are absent, and mic_problem carries the sentence (the note repeats it). THE GRANTS: this tool never asks for one and never opens the picker. The Screen Recording grant (and the Microphone grant when microphone is true, and the Camera grant for source camera or a camera beside the screen) must already be held by this process — the panel is where somebody grants them — and a missing one is refused by name with the System Settings pane in the sentence. A Frame Job launched from a shell runs under the TERMINAL's grants, not the app icon's, and both refusals then also name the launching process (its pid) and the way out — relaunch with open -a "Frame Job", or grant the terminal. THE REFUSAL ORDER is fixed: your own mistakes first (seconds missing or outside 1…600, a source outside the vocabulary and the arguments that source refuses, display and window both given, a rate or size outside the vocabulary, enhance: true without a microphone and then with place: false, auto_zoom, shortcut_overlays and speed_up_typing each with place: false and the last two without keys: shortcuts, a camera_layout outside the vocabulary, camera_layout and then camera_cutout: true with place: false, microphone: true without the Microphone grant, a project naming nothing open), then for a camera recording or a camera beside the screen the camera lookup, then its camera_format, then the Camera grant, then for a screen recording the Screen Recording grant, then the display or window lookup — where a console that is locked or asleep lists NO display and is refused as that, by name; then the recording itself. While it records, a status item in the menu bar shows the elapsed time with a menu offering Pause Recording and Stop Recording — Resume Recording and Stop Recording while it is paused — and File ▸ Pause Recording (Resume Recording while paused) and File ▸ Stop Recording work too. A person's Stop from the menu bar or the File menu ends an agent's recording EARLY and it still lands, with stopped_by: stopped — the same value the tool's own stop at the span's end yields — and a duration shorter than the span, which is what says so; user_stopped is only the SYSTEM's own screen-recording indicator, and system_stopped a display that slept or a camera that stopped on its own. PAUSE: the span is wall clock, so a person's pause SHORTENS what the call records — the paused stretch is in no file — and the result's pauses says how many times Pause was pressed (0 when never; a pause with no resume before the stop still counts). A paused recording is a SEQUENCE of files, one per stretch between a start or resume and a pause or the stop, each named by its own start time and, with a microphone, carrying its own microphone file with its own measured mic_offset; every segment lands as its own clip placed at the previous one's end on ONE track, touching and never overlapping, and each microphone file as its own clip on the Microphone track at its own offset. segments carries one entry per file (exactly one for an unpaused recording) and duration is the TOTAL recorded across them. A segment whose movie will not read (an empty file, from a pause in the instant after a resume), or whose writer failed after the segment closed, is LEFT OUT rather than failing the recording: the readable segments land, and the result's unreadable lists each one left out — path, kept_files (what it left on disk), reason, and mic_path, mic_duration, mic_media and mic_clip when its microphone file reads, which lands without its picture in the slot the picture would have had — with the note naming them; only a recording with NO readable movie fails, naming every file. The call blocks for seconds plus about a second of start and finish, and up to 75 s more if the writers are slow to close the files — 60 s more for each further segment of a paused recording, whose files are probed in turn; a timeout names the movies, which may still finish on their own. THE RESULT carries: path (the FIRST segment's movie — the recording's file, the one a new project is addressed by); mic_offset (ALWAYS present — the first segment's, 0 without a microphone); mic_path and mic_duration (the first segment's) when its microphone file landed, and mic_problem — every segment's sentence, joined — when a microphone was asked for and any segment's did not land, which can stand beside a mic_path when it was a later segment's; media and clip (the first segment's ids; clip and mic_clip absent with place: false), mic_media and mic_clip (its microphone's); duration (ticks — the TOTAL recorded, every segment's summed, which for an unpaused recording is the movie's own); width, height, fps [num, den], has_audio and audio_tracks — the FIRST segment's movie's (what it holds: audio_tracks is 1 with system_audio, else 0 — the microphone is never a track of it); pauses (an integer, the count of Pause presses); segments (an array, ALWAYS present, one entry per file in order, each with path, duration, started_at — the screen's own start as an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp to the millisecond — its OWN width, height and fps, because a screen recording's rate is whatever the screen did and differs per segment, and mic_path, mic_duration, mic_offset and mic_problem on the same terms as the top level for THAT segment's files, plus media, clip, mic_media and mic_clip when they are known); stopped_by — stopped for the tool's own stop and for a person's Stop from Frame Job's menu-bar item or the File menu, user_stopped for the system's own screen-recording indicator, system_stopped for a display that slept or a camera that stopped on its own; landed (document or new_project); note, when there is something to say; project, the usual summary; and for a document landing the created ids as every edit reports them — new_media, new_clips, and new_tracks when a track was minted — plus scope and document_ops when it landed inside a nest. A failure AFTER the files were written names every one of them: "The recording was saved at <path> but could not be added: …", the movies comma-separated and the microphone files after them. UNDO: for a document landing, undo removes every segment's media and clip(s) in ONE step and leaves the files on disk, as undoing Add Media… does; a recording that opened as a new project has no undo step for its first segment — that picture IS the document — and with a microphone on an unpaused recording, undo removes the microphone pair (the step is named Add Microphone) and leaves the picture, while a PAUSED recording's later segments and every microphone clip are one step named Add Recording Segments, so undo leaves the first picture alone in the document. A VOICE-OVER: source: "voice_over" records the DEFAULT microphone alone — the panel's Source row Microphone Only — with no picture, into files named Voice-over <date> at <time>.m4a, one file per stretch between pauses. Every file lands touching, from the playhead, on ONE new back track named Microphone, in one undo step (Add Recording); as a new project the first file IS the document, 1920×1080 at rate, and the later files touch it on its one track. display, window, system_audio, show_clicks, size and include_framejob_windows are refused by name with source voice_over, and so is microphone: false (true is implied); source is read right after seconds, and only the Microphone grant is read — never the Screen Recording one. The result's path is the first .m4a, its width and height 0, with no mic_path, and mic_offset 0; a microphone that stops on its own ends the voice-over, what it wrote lands, and mic_problem and the note say so. A CAMERA: source: "camera" records a camera alone, with no screen — the one camera names (a device's unique id, or its name in any case), else the default camera (the system's preferred camera, else the first built-in, else the first) — at its best format (the largest size wider than tall at 30 fps or more, at that format's highest rate) or the one camera_format names (a format the camera lacks is refused naming its formats), into files named Camera Recording <date> at <time>.mov, one file per stretch between pauses; microphone: true adds the DEFAULT microphone as a second file, as for a screen. It lands as a screen recording's picture does; as a new project the canvas is the file's size at the format's rate, rounded. display, window, system_audio, show_clicks, size, include_framejob_windows and rate are refused by name with source camera, and camera and camera_format with source voice_over. The camera is looked up after project — an unknown one is refused naming every camera connected, and "No camera is connected." when there is none — and only then is the Camera grant read, never the Screen Recording one. The span counts from the camera's first frame, after it settles at its rate (up to a second). The result carries camera: {name, id, format, problem, note} — format spelled 1920x1080@30; camera.problem the sentence of a camera that stopped on its own, which ends the recording with stopped_by: system_stopped and lands what it wrote; camera.note when the camera had not settled at its rate when the recording began; each of the two also said in the note — and has_audio false: the movie holds no sound. A CAMERA BESIDE THE SCREEN: source: "screen" (the default) with camera records that camera at the same time as the screen — camera_format as for source camera, refused without camera — one <movie stem> (Camera).mov per segment beside each movie. The camera files land in the same undo step, on ONE new track named Camera in FRONT of the screen's, one clip per segment at its screen clip's start plus that segment's camera_offset (ticks, positive when the camera began after the screen; it is usually negative, a camera starting first, and then the clip's head is trimmed rather than the clip placed early), never before its screen clip and never overlapping the camera clip before it. Each camera clip lands in camera_layout's layout by one switch_layout at its first frame, one frame long, with its segment's screen clip as the screen and reaching no further than the later of the two clips' ends: corner_square (the default) is the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner — scaled to fit a quarter of the canvas wide and a third of it tall, inside the 90 % safe-area ring — and a segment whose screen clip is missing or does not play at the camera's start gets that corner by set_video x, y and scale instead; either way it stays an ordinary clip to move. With camera_cutout: true the camera clips then get Remove Background as their own undo step before any enhance, and the answer carries camera_cutout {clips} or camera_cutout_error, the sentence when no camera clip landed. The microphone, when asked for, is its own file on the Microphone track as for any screen recording. With place: false the camera files are media with no clip and no Camera track. As a new project the first movie is the document and the camera lands in its remainder step — named Add Camera, or Add Camera and Microphone with a voice, for one segment. Each entry of segments then also carries camera_path, camera_duration and camera_offset when that segment's camera file landed, camera_problem and camera_note when set (also said in the note), and camera_media and camera_clip when known; the top-level camera is as for source camera. A segment left out because its movie will not read keeps its camera file on disk, named in its kept_files, and does not land it. The stop wait allows 105 s, and 90 s more for each further segment, because the camera's file is probed too, and a timeout names the camera files after the movies. The recorder panel's Record the camera too box, with a display or a window, makes the same recording, and its Layout pop-up and Remove the camera's background when it lands box are camera_layout and camera_cutout. ENHANCE: enhance: true runs enhance_voice over the recording's MICROPHONE clips — each segment's microphone file, or a voice-over's files; never the picture, a camera or the system audio — once their loudness and speech have been analysed, at −16 LUFS, as its OWN undo step named Enhance Voice after the landing's (undo takes the processing off and keeps the recording). The call waits for that analysis, up to 5 minutes, and the answer then also carries enhance — enhance_voice's own answer — or enhance_error, a sentence saying why it did not run (nothing measurable, no microphone clip on the timeline, or not analysed within 5 minutes); project is read after it. The landing itself is the same either way. The recorder panel's Enhance the microphone when it lands box does the same. CURSOR: every display, window or picked recording also writes the pointer's path, clicks, scrolls and the frames' geometry beside each segment movie as <movie stem>.fjcursor (the pointer is still in the picture too). Each entry of segments then also carries cursor_path and cursor_image ("none": no cursor image is recorded) when that segment's cursor file was written, and cursor_problem when it was not or holds only the geometry the screen had when the segment began (also said in the note); a cursor problem never fails the recording. WHEN IT LANDS: auto_zoom, shortcut_overlays and speed_up_typing run auto_zoom, add_shortcut_overlays and speed_up_typing over the recording's SCREEN clips (each segment's movie whose media has a cursor file) after the landing and after any enhance, in that order, each as its OWN undo step named Auto Zoom, Add Shortcut Overlays and Speed Up Typing, with those tools' defaults and no from or to. speed_up_typing waits for the clips' speech to be detected, up to 5 minutes. The answer then also carries each one's own answer under its name, or a sentence under <name>_error saying why it did not run (no screen clip with a cursor file, the project busy or the speech not detected within 5 minutes, the call stopped, or the tool's own refusal); project is read after them. The recorder panel's When it lands boxes — Zoom in on clicks, Show shortcuts and Speed up typing — do the same.

1	import Foundation
     2	
     3	/// A recording's cursor file over MCP (road map "creator-jobs" CU5, spec §11
     4	/// CU-50, CU-53): the op tool `set_media_cursor`, which mirrors the Media
     5	/// tab's Cursor section ▸ Locate… and Remove (`MediaPane+Cursor.swift`), and
     6	/// `get_cursor_events`, a read with no menu: the file's clicks, scrolls,
     7	/// shortcuts, typing stretches and path, in media or clip time.
     8	extension AgentServer {
     9	
    10	    // MARK: - set_media_cursor
    11	
    12	    /// `set_media_cursor` — Locate… and Remove. A non-null `cursor` is held
    13	    /// to Locate's own check first (CU-50 (b)): the file opens through the
    14	    /// core and its `movie_size` is the movie's (`cursorAttachment`, CU-34),
    15	    /// and the call's `in_picture` is the file's. The path checked is the
    16	    /// path stored, as given (no `~` expansion). Passing both, the op is
    17	    /// sent with the caller's value as given; the core reads it strictly and
    18	    /// refuses by name. An unknown media goes on to the core's own sentence;
    19	    /// `null` is not checked.
    20	    func setMediaCursor(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
    21	        let document = try target(a)
    22	        let media = try idArg(a, "media")
    23	        guard let cursor = a["cursor"] else {
    24	            throw ToolError(
    25	                message: "Missing required argument: cursor ({path, bookmark?, in_picture} or "
    26	                    + "null)")
    27	        }
    28	        if let object = cursor as? [String: Any],
    29	            let path = object["path"] as? String, !path.isEmpty,
    30	            let entry = document.project.snapshot.media(media)
    31	        {
    32	            let file = URL(fileURLWithPath: path)
    33	            switch MediaImporter.cursorAttachment(at: file, to: MediaDescriptor(entry)) {
    34	            case .failure(let problem):
    35	                throw ToolError(message: problem.message)
    36	            case .success(let attachment):
    37	                if let asked = object["in_picture"] as? Bool,
    38	                    asked != attachment.cursor.inPicture
    39	                {
    40	                    throw ToolError(
    41	                        message: "The cursor file \(file.lastPathComponent) was not attached: "
    42	                            + "its in_picture is \(attachment.cursor.inPicture) and the call "
    43	                            + "says \(asked).")
    44	                }
    45	            }
    46	        }
    47	        let name = cursor is NSNull ? "Remove Cursor File" : "Locate Cursor File"
    48	        return try editResult(
    49	            document, name, [.setMediaCursorRaw(media: media, cursor: cursor)],
    50	            ["media": Int(media)])
    51	    }
    52	
    53	    // MARK: - get_cursor_events
    54	
    55	    /// What the first main-thread hop resolves.
    56	    struct CursorEventsCall {
    57	        let document: ProjectDocument
    58	        let media: MediaSnapshot
    59	        let clip: ClipSnapshot?
    60	        let times: AnalysisClipTimes?
    61	        let file: URL
    62	        let request: CursorEventsAnswer.Request
    63	    }
    64	
    65	    /// `get_cursor_events` — refused in CU-53 (g)'s order. **Runs on the
    66	    /// SERVER thread** (`creatorOffMainTools`): one main hop resolves, the
    67	    /// file is opened as a fresh `ReelCursor` here, and a last main hop
    68	    /// computes Q, which reads `clip_state`, and the summary.
    69	    func getCursorEvents(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
    70	        guard !Thread.isMainThread else {
    71	            throw ToolError(
    72	                message: "get_cursor_events must run on the server thread — its name is "
    73	                    + "missing from AgentServer.creatorOffMainTools.")
    74	        }
    75	        let call = try onMain { try self.resolveCursorEventsCall(a) }
    76	        let track: ReelCursor
    77	        let read: CursorEventsAnswer.Read
    78	        do {
    79	            track = try ReelCursor(data: try Data(contentsOf: call.file))
    80	            read = try CursorEventsAnswer.read(track, call.request, times: call.times)
    81	        } catch {
    82	            let reason = (error as? ReelCoreError)?.message ?? error.localizedDescription
    83	            throw ToolError(
    84	                message: "The cursor file \(call.file.lastPathComponent) could not be read: "
    85	                    + reason)
    86	        }
    87	        return try onMain {
    88	            var result = CursorEventsAnswer.answer(
    89	                read, call.request, crop: { t in self.cropAt(call, clipTime: t) })
    90	            result["media"] = Int(call.media.id)
    91	            if let clip = call.clip { result["clip"] = Int(clip.id) }
    92	            result["size"] = [call.media.width, call.media.height]
    93	            result["cursor_file"] = call.file.path
    94	            result["in_picture"] = call.media.cursor?.inPicture ?? false
    95	            result["project"] = self.summary(call.document)
    96	            return try self.jsonResult(result)
    97	        }
    98	    }
    99	
   100	    /// The clip's crop at clip tick `t` (CU-53 (c)): its base crop when it
   101	    /// has no actions, else `clip_state`'s at `clip.start + t` on the edited
   102	    /// project. Main thread.
   103	    private func cropAt(_ call: CursorEventsCall, clipTime t: Ticks) -> CropInsets {
   104	        guard let clip = call.clip else { return CropInsets() }
   105	        guard !clip.actions.isEmpty else { return clip.videoProps.crop }
   106	        let state = call.document.editedProject.clipState(clip.id, at: clip.start + t)
   107	        let crop = (state?["video"] as? [String: Any])?["crop"] as? [String: Any]
   108	        func side(_ key: String) -> Double { (crop?[key] as? NSNumber)?.doubleValue ?? 0 }
   109	        return CropInsets(l: side("l"), t: side("t"), r: side("r"), b: side("b"))
   110	    }
   111	
   112	    private func resolveCursorEventsCall(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> CursorEventsCall {
   113	        func given(_ key: String) -> Bool { a[key] != nil && !(a[key] is NSNull) }
   114	        guard given("media") != given("clip") else {
   115	            throw ToolError(
   116	                message: "Name exactly one of media and clip: the recording whose cursor file "
   117	                    + "to read in its own times, or the clip to read it in clip time.")
   118	        }
   119	        let kinds = try CursorEventsAnswer.kinds(try stringsArg(a, "kinds"))
   120	        let smoothingArg = try doubleArg(a, "smoothing")
   121	        if let s = smoothingArg, !(0...1).contains(s) {
   122	            throw ToolError(message: "smoothing must be 0–1, not \(s).")
   123	        }
   124	        let document = try target(a)
   125	        let media: MediaSnapshot
   126	        var clip: ClipSnapshot?
   127	        var times: AnalysisClipTimes?
   128	        if given("clip") {
   129	            let snapshot = try clipArg(a, "clip", document)
   130	            guard case .media(let id, _, _) = snapshot.source,
   131	                let entry = document.editedProject.snapshot.media(id)
   132	            else {
   133	                throw ToolError(
   134	                    message: "Clip \(snapshot.id) is not a media clip (it shows "
   135	                        + "\(snapshot.source.kindName)), so it has no cursor file.")
   136	            }

   185	            throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
   186	        }

   188	            throw ToolError(message: "Wrote \(url.path) but could not read it back.")
   189	        }
