   246	    /// One graphic's report as `render_frame` says it: failed at a frame,
   247	    /// did not compile, or warned — each diagnostic with its location.
   248	    static func graphicSentence(_ report: GraphicReport) -> String {
   249	        let said = report.diagnostics.map { $0.located }.joined(separator: "; ")
   250	        guard let frame = report.frame else {
   251	            return "Graphic \"\(report.name)\" does not compile: \(said)."
   252	        }
   253	        let verb = report.failed ? "failed" : "warned"
   254	        return "Graphic \"\(report.name)\" \(verb) at frame \(frame): \(said)."
   255	    }
   256	
   257	    /// Where `render_frame` writes and in what container — its `path` and
   258	    /// `format` arguments resolved together, because neither can be read
   259	    /// without the other.
   260	    ///
   261	    /// **No `path` is the case every proof script takes**, and it is exactly
   262	    /// what it was: a file in the temporary directory named for the tick it
   263	    /// holds, ending in the format's own extension — `.png` unless a caller
   264	    /// asked for something else.
   265	    ///
   266	    /// With a `path`, the format is `FrameWriter`'s answer and not a second
   267	    /// opinion: an explicit `format` wins, else the path's own extension, else
   268	    /// PNG — `export_captions`' rule, one file over. The path then goes
   269	    /// through `destinationURL`, so a wrong extension is REPLACED rather than
   270	    /// appended to: `{path: "shot.jpg", format: "png"}` writes `shot.png`, not
   271	    /// the doubled `shot.jpg.png`, which is why the five image containers
   272	    /// joined `replaceableExtensions` in this phase.
   273	    ///
   274	    /// The folder must already exist and is refused BY NAME when it does not,
   275	    /// which is `export`'s posture at the same point: a tool that created
   276	    /// directories would answer a mistyped path by scattering empty ones.
   277	    private func frameDestination(
   278	        _ a: [String: Any], at time: Ticks
   279	    ) throws -> (url: URL, format: FrameWriter.Format) {
   280	        let requested = try requestedFrameFormat(a)
   281	        guard let given = try stringArg(a, "path") else {
   282	            let format = requested ?? .png
   283	            return (
   284	                Self.temporaryOutput("framejob-frame-\(time)", extension: format.fileExtension),
   285	                format
   286	            )
   287	        }
   288	        let path = try Self.nonEmptyOutputPath(given)
   289	        let format = FrameWriter.format(
   290	            for: URL(fileURLWithPath: (path as NSString).expandingTildeInPath),
   291	            requested: requested)
   292	        let url = try Self.requireFolder(
   293	            of: Self.destinationURL(path, extension: format.fileExtension))
   294	        return (url, format)
   295	    }
   296	
   297	    /// The `format` argument, refused BY NAME when it names no container —
   298	    /// nil when it is absent, which is what lets `FrameWriter.format(for:)`
   299	    /// fall back to the path. It is `export_captions`' `requestedFormat` with
   300	    /// three rows instead of two.
   301	    ///
   302	    /// `jpg` is read as `jpeg` on purpose. `FrameWriter.Format`'s raw value is
   303	    /// deliberately NOT its file extension — JPEG has two spellings and
   304	    /// collapsing them would make one of them wrong — and `format(for:)`
   305	    /// already reads both off a path, so refusing four letters here that are
   306	    /// accepted in the argument beside it is an inconsistency a caller meets
   307	    /// on its first try. The schema still advertises the three canonical
   308	    /// names, which is what a caller reading the catalog will send.
   309	    private func requestedFrameFormat(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> FrameWriter.Format? {
   310	        guard let name = try stringArg(a, "format") else { return nil }
   311	        let lowered = name.lowercased()
   312	        guard let format = FrameWriter.Format(rawValue: lowered == "jpg" ? "jpeg" : lowered)
   313	        else {
   314	            let known = FrameWriter.Format.allCases.map { $0.rawValue }
   315	            throw ToolError(
   316	                message: "format must be one of " + known.joined(separator: ", ")
   317	                    + " (got \"\(name)\").")
   318	        }
   319	        return format
   320	    }
   321	
   322	    /// The image block's `mimeType`, read off the format's own `UTType`
   323	    /// rather than switched over a second time here: the block and the file
   324	    /// are then one decision, and a fourth container would arrive described
   325	    /// correctly without anybody remembering this line.
   326	    ///
   327	    /// All three carry one (measured: `image/png`, `image/jpeg`,
   328	    /// `image/heic`). The fallback exists only because the API is optional,
   329	    /// and it is deliberately generic rather than a guess: telling a client
   330	    /// that a HEIC is a PNG is worse than telling it nothing.
   331	    private static func mimeType(_ format: FrameWriter.Format) -> String {
   332	        format.contentType.preferredMIMEType ?? "application/octet-stream"
   333	    }

`export` takes `preset` and `path`, plus `size`, `range` (`project` or
`in_out`), `video_bitrate`, `audio_bitrate`, `audio_bits`, `loudness_lufs`, `peak_dbtp`,
`burn_in_timecode`, `dynamic_range`, `encoder_speed` and `stems`. The presets are `h264`, `hevc`,
`hevc_alpha`, `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `vp9_alpha_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`, `audio_m4a`,
`audio_wav`, `audio_aiff`, `gif` and `apng`. There is no frame-rate
argument: an export runs at the project's rate, or at 12.5 fps for `gif` and
25 fps for `apng`. An existing file at the path is replaced, and the
format's extension is added when the path has none. `peak_dbtp` (−20 to 0)
is the ceiling of the limiter every export with sound goes through, −1 dBTP
when absent, and may be given with or without `loudness_lufs`. `audio_bits`
(16 or 24, 16 when absent) is `audio_wav`'s and `audio_aiff`'s alone and is
refused on every other preset. `stems` (`tracks` or `names`) is the three
audio presets' alone: it also writes one file per heard track, or per track
name, beside the mix, each its tracks' sound before the master, replacing any
file at its name; it is refused on every other preset and when no track can
be heard, the job fails when a stem's file would be one of the project's
media, and the done answer lists each as `stems [{name, tracks, path}]`
([Stems](export.md#stems)). `dynamic_range` `hlg` or `pq` is refused outside
`hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422` and `prores_4444` (so on
`vp9_alpha_webm`, always 8-bit), and in an SDR project.
`encoder_speed` (`faster`, `balanced` or `smaller`) is `av1`'s and `av1_webm`'s
alone and is refused on every other preset, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm` (one speed)
included; the done answer names it. On those two and `vp9_webm`, `video_bitrate` is a soft
cap: the file usually comes in well under it, and very detailed footage can go
up to about 1.25 times over it on AV1 and about 1.15 times on VP9. On `vp9_alpha_webm` it
is the same soft cap on the picture's stream alone, and the alpha stream comes on top of it
(about 6–15 % of the video at 1080p, up to about 39 % at 640 × 360, measured). `vp9_alpha_webm`
keeps a transparent canvas, as `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha` and `apng` do, and refuses a
`[width, height]` of another shape. What each option means is in [Export](export.md).

`get_project` answers the whole project as JSON, the same document every op
edits:

- **`project`** — the canvas (width, height, fps as `[num, den]`, background,

  `tracks`, `clips`, `markers`, `nests` (each with its own tracks and clips)
  and `next_id`.
- **The app's own state**, which is not saved in the project: `playhead`,
